sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up, with the largest increases above roughly 0.76.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises as delinquencies accumulate, though the step from one to two or more is the main change.
The two drivers reinforce each other: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two or more past delinquencies than for those with none.
Annual income has a moderate effect, with lower income raising predicted risk and higher income lowering it.
Length of credit history has a moderate effect, with longer histories lowering predicted risk.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak to moderate effect, with higher ratios raising predicted risk.
Age and months at the current address have negligible effects, and the data do not settle whether the number of dependents has any effect at all.
The number of recent credit inquiries has at most a weak effect, and the data do not settle whether higher counts raise risk.
